rationale: The official PMC landing page identifies olanzapine in a Huntington case and points to a PDF-only body. The official PDF response was an interstitial and the cloud counterpart was unavailable.
The author abstract verifies a review of 307 Wilson disease records. The linked body PDF is still unverified. Preserve the case-level exposure and outcome scope at abstract depth.
The author abstract compares stimulation and medication among 39 Parkinson participants. The linked body did not resolve to PDF. The full methods and individual symptom outcomes remain open.
The case describes drooling during acute pediatric poststreptococcal dystonia, with serial striatal MRI figures. Case management and images supply no oral fig exposure.

One of two reported 22q11.2-deletion patients had drooling before levodopa. The figures depict clinical appearance and imaging. The clinical histories contain no fig exposure or dietary treatment comparison.

The case describes severe chronic drooling and perioral dermatitis in Parkinson disease. The figure depicts the dermatitis. Reported change followed salivary-gland treatment, with no raw fig exposure.

The six face-transplant cases concern postoperative fluid collections and interventions. Salivary leakage was a surgical complication and the figure panels depict imaging. No raw fig or Parkinson exposure comparison.

This is a Parkinson patient-reported symptom instrument and score-validation study. The figure concerns scale relationships, and drooling contributes symptom vocabulary rather than screening any fig intervention.

The Persian SWAL-QOL validation compares swallowing-related questionnaire scores and psychometrics. Food selection is a questionnaire domain. The article does not compare raw fig intake or Parkinson drooling.
The patient had drooling and parkinsonian features with osmotic demyelination. The dietary history concerns alcohol, and the fig abbreviation labels MRI images. The case supplies no fig ingestion.

The imaging study reports comparable drooling scores in Parkinson patients with and without hyposmia in its clinical table. It measures magnetic susceptibility and nonmotor symptoms, with no raw fig exposure.

The Parkinson case tests oral levodopa transport before and after tongue training. Jelly of unspecified composition accompanied both tests. The figures report swallowing and drug levels, with no raw fig or separate drooling response.

The original correlates enteric alpha-synuclein findings and gastrointestinal symptoms in Parkinson and control participants. The symptom questionnaire includes drooling. No fig-specific exposure or assigned food contrast was reported.

The manometry and endoscopy study compares Parkinsonian disorders. Named test materials include puree, colored liquid and white bread. The methods do not identify fig or report a raw fig and drooling comparison.
The three ATP1A3 cases describe neurological phenotypes and dysphagia with diverse clinical histories. The management and family data do not identify raw fig ingestion.

The body reports a 163-item food questionnaire and separate sialorrhea scores. The official 111-page supplement gives grouped fruit measures and imports a separate dietary input. No published raw-fig exposure or fig-by-drooling estimate was identified.
The two-sibling VAC14 evaluation describes genetic and clinical findings. Its case narratives and figure captions supply no raw fig treatment or Parkinson drooling comparison.
The case describes a Wilson disease tongue movement followed by penicillamine treatment. The video and image material illustrate the movement, with no raw fig comparison.
The report contrasts movement phenotypes in relatives with spinocerebellar ataxia type 2. Clinical management differs between relatives, and neither case studies raw fig.
The Wilson disease case includes drooling with hypertrophic olivary degeneration. Its figure depicts MRI. No raw fig exposure is described.
Remote deep brain stimulation programming is the exposure. The preliminary Parkinson series records nonmotor assessments, with no assigned food or raw fig comparison.
The pooled placebo-controlled amantadine trials include an exploratory saliva and drooling item. The actual intervention is amantadine, with no dietary fig arm.

A mitochondrial variant was identified by reanalysis of sequencing and evaluated in the clinical case and family context. Orofacial signs and figures concern diagnostic phenotyping. No raw fig exposure.

The Parkinson motor-phenotype study records self-perceived speech, voice and swallowing symptoms. Saliva and drooling are symptom questionnaire context. Nothing in the methods assigns or compares raw fig.
The protocol plans an intensive voice intervention and repeated drooling measurements for children with cerebral palsy. There are no outcome results or raw fig exposure in the protocol.

The pediatric cobalamin case reports neurological decline and dribbling before post-treatment movement findings. Vitamin treatment and clinical assessment provide no raw fig exposure or Parkinson outcome.
The case concerns probable progressive supranuclear palsy and prior antipsychotic treatment. The clinical chronology and images provide no raw fig exposure.
The Parkinson study compares corneal nerve microscopy by autonomic involvement. Salivary items contribute to autonomic scoring. The imaging and symptom analysis does not capture raw fig.
The Parkinson outreach study evaluates a provider education program. Drooling is a topic in nonmotor care. There is no assigned food or raw fig clinical comparison.
The ALS case measures salivary symptoms around radiation treatment. Its assessment references a Parkinson-derived scale but supplies no raw fig exposure.
The avapritinib case reports sialorrhea during a severe parkinsonian syndrome. The timeline concerns prescribed agents and systemic illness without a reported fig exposure.

The veterinary report evaluates cannabidiol in one horse with crib-biting. Prior dietary modifications are historical care context. No raw fig was identified and the clinical outcome is an equine behavior.

The matched cross-sectional study separately measures drooling burden and salivary output. The Parkinson cohort has more drooling with lower average salivary flow. No dietary fig comparison was performed.

Parkinson participants with and without restless legs had different swallowing questionnaire scores and no clear difference on the sialorrhea scale. Restless legs status is the exposure and raw fig is absent.
The TUBB2B family report includes drooling in one affected child. Figure and video references document mirror movements and imaging, with no raw fig exposure.
The Parkinson mild cognitive impairment classifier uses imaging, gait, eye-tracking and clinical scale inputs. Saliva or nonmotor variables do not identify an oral fig comparison.
Parkinson participants discuss saliva pooling and a wearable swallowing cue in a qualitative interview. The quoted discussion does not test a raw fig exposure or establish an intervention effect.

The case evaluates pharyngeal electrical stimulation after brainstem stroke. The swallowed test material was ice chips and the assessed endpoints included secretion control and aspiration. No fig exposure.
